newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks end up, demand outstrips supply.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks end up, demand outstrips supply.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed slightly higher on Tuesday as buyers paid premiums for small number of shares due to lack of liquidity, brokers said.
The Colombo Stock Exchange all share index closed 3.01 points higher at 611.01.
"The market is up due to a lack of sellers," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena of Commercial Stock Brokers.

"Sellers are holding on because they feel the market will go up by at least a few points in the coming weeks. Buyers have started to pay premium prices for whatever quantity that is available, also for the same reason," he said.

Brokers say expectations of good corporate growth in 1997 have improved market sentiment. Sri Lankan stocks, which ended last year on an upbeat note, have gained more than six points in the first week of trading in the new year.
Turnover was a modest 16.2 million rupees, but was higher than Monday's 14.8 million rupees.
DFCC was up by 10 rupees to 270 rupees, Ceylon Tobacco 1.50 rupees to 31.50, Commercial Bank one rupee to 131. Hatton National Bank fell 10 rupees to 250 rupees.
